home.title: What is any website built with, and how big is it?
home.subtitle: Enter a domain to see its tech stack, hosting, email and SSL setup, and an honest traffic range.
home.f1b: CMS, frameworks, analytics, CDN, email, payments and more. Each detection shows the header, script or DNS record that gave it away.
home.f2b: Nobody but the owner knows exact traffic. We combine public popularity signals and show a range, never a fake-precise number.
home.f3b: Site owners will be able to connect analytics to show exact numbers. Those sites also calibrate estimates for everyone else.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.description: How we detect technologies and estimate website traffic, and how accurate it is.
methodology.intro: We want every number on this site to be honest. Here is exactly where it comes from.
methodology.techP: We fetch the homepage like a browser would. We look for fingerprints in HTTP headers, cookies, HTML, script URLs, meta tags, DNS records (MX, NS, TXT) and the SSL certificate. The fingerprints come from the community-maintained, open Wappalyzer-format database ({count} technologies). Each detection on a report lists the evidence we found. We respect robots.txt.
methodology.trafficP1: Only a site's owner knows its exact traffic. Everyone else, including large paid tools, estimates it. Independent tests have found average errors around 50% even for the biggest tools, and much worse for small sites.
methodology.trafficP2: We use public popularity lists that are licensed for commercial use:
methodology.trafficP3: Each list's rank is converted to visits with a model of the form log(visits) = a + b · log(rank). When several lists cover a site we combine them; when they disagree, the range gets wider. We show a range covering roughly two out of three cases. If a site is not in any list, we say there is not enough data instead of inventing a number.
methodology.calYes: The model was fitted on real traffic data on {date}. {note}
methodology.calNo: The model is not calibrated yet. It uses rough default assumptions, so treat estimates as approximate orders of magnitude.
methodology.modelP: We don't see a site's analytics, so pages per visit, visit duration and bounce rate are industry benchmarks for the kind of site we detect, clearly labelled as typical rather than measured:
methodology.earnP: Display-ad revenue = pageviews × revenue per 1,000 pageviews (RPM) × share not ad-blocked. RPM depends on where visitors are: ${t1} for the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Northern Europe; ${t2} for the rest of Europe, Japan, Korea and the Gulf; ${t3} for India and most other markets; ${mix} when we don't know. We assume {block}% of pageviews are ad-blocked.
methodology.earnP2: If we detect an ad network (such as Google AdSense) we call it estimated ad revenue; if not, ad potential, because the site probably earns in other ways. Worth is {months} months of that revenue, a common range for content sites. For stores and software products it is only a floor.
methodology.earnP3: Every step has a range. We combine them the statistically correct way (in log space), so ranges stay useful instead of multiplying worst cases together.
methodology.verifiedP: Site owners will be able to connect Google Analytics or Search Console to show exact numbers with a Verified badge. Verified sites are also used to calibrate estimates for everyone else.
